symbols.name: lexicalTokens
doc: Announcements are short, born-digital text (title + contentText), each with a single whole-record embedding (no chunking, no pages). I mirror the circular content engine's hybrid approach here: vector similarity OR a literal match on the plain-text body/title, but against one row per announcement.

Returns rows tagged `type: "announcement"`, shaped like every other SearchResultRow so the router can merge them with circulars transparently. The words of a question, found wherever they stand in a passage. A person asks "OTP valid for five minutes" and the PDF says "OTPs remain valid for only five minutes": the phrase is not there as typed, and a long passage that holds other things as well is only a little like the question in meaning, so neither the substring match nor the vector finds it. What does is the circulars' own test: I look for the question's content words (not "what", "the", "for") in the passage, and the passage counts when it holds most of them. `lexicalTokens` are those words; `isLexicalHit` is the test.

symbols.name: wordsFound
symbols.sig: export function wordsFound(tokens: string[], text: string): number
doc: Counts how many of the words stand in the text (a word counts inside a longer one: "otp" in "OTPs").

symbols.name: isLexicalHit
symbols.sig: export function isLexicalHit(tokens: string[], text: string): boolean
doc: My rule for two or more words: at least two of them and at least 60% of them. For one word: that word, if it has 4 letters or more.

symbols.name: orTsQuery
doc: Turns the words into a Postgres text-search query: any of them (the stricter test is isLexicalHit); only letters and digits go in.

symbols.name: PdfChunkHit
doc: One passage of an announcement that matched (announcement_chunk: its own text, or its PDF), as the database returns it.

members.name: source
doc: Where the passage is: the announcement's own text, or its PDF.

symbols.name: mergeAnnouncementHits
symbols.sig: export function mergeAnnouncementHits(records: RecordRow[], chunks: PdfChunkHit[]): Array<SearchResultRow & { internalScore: number }>
doc: I put the passages that matched (of an announcement's own text, and of its PDF) together with the announcements that matched by their title and body: ONE row for each announcement, whichever way it was found, ranked by its best score. A PDF passage that is the best evidence (a literal hit, or a stronger vector than the title and body gave) becomes the row's text, with its page (the window opens the PDF there) and `matchInPdf` set. Same rule as the record's own: a passage counts if it holds the words, or is strongly similar (0.6).
